prompt.context: Your client, Sosland (pronounced sauce-land) Sports, is an operator of squash centers in Sweden. The squash centers include sauna, spa, pool, gym and — of course — the squash courts! Due to the extreme success in Sweden, the company is considering expanding to other countries in Europe, in particular Germany. The founder and CEO, Felicity Sosland, has asked us to evaluate this possible expansion.
prompt.question: What factors would you consider in order to estimate the outcomes of this expansion?

clarifying_info.q: What type of centers does Sosland Sports operate?
clarifying_info.a: Sosland Sports centers are mid-range centers with medium-quality facilities. They only exist in Sweden.

clarifying_info.q: What is the goal of the expansion?
clarifying_info.a: The goal is to at least break even. There is no specific timeframe.

exhibits.title: Cost overview
exhibits.shows: A table summarizing the key operating parameters for a single squash center in Germany.

framework: Customers: market size and growth rate, market segmentation (activity level, ages), cultural factors (German sporting preferences)
Competitors: number and concentration, substitutes, competitive intensity, positioning
Company: replication of business model, economies of scale, cost of expansion, projected profitability

questions.prompt: Develop a problem-solving structure and describe how you would gather the data needed.
questions.guidance: Best approached using a 3C's or Five Forces framework. Candidate should identify Customers (market size, segmentation, cultural factors), Competitors (number, intensity, positioning, substitutes), and Company (business model replication, economies of scale, cost and profitability). For data gathering, strong answers distinguish between internal sources (firm resources, client's own organization) and external sources (market research reports, internet research on competitors, real estate agents for cost data, colleagues with local market experience).

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit A, determine the minimum annual membership fee Sosland Sports must charge to cover running costs.
questions.guidance: Candidate should work through: hours available, utilization, mix of singles vs doubles to find total members, then divide cost by members. Strong candidate will note the €90.70 annual fee seems low and proactively compare it against the competition. Outstanding candidate solves it cleanly and immediately contextualizes the number relative to the client problem.

math.setup: Annual cost = €200,000. Need to find members at 70% utilization, 15 courts, 10 operating hours/day, 7 days/week, assuming 50% singles (2 players) and 50% doubles (4 players).
steps: Hours available per week = 10 hours/day × 7 days/week × 15 courts = 1,050 hours
math.answer: ~€90.70 per member per year (this is an annual fee, not a weekly fee)

questions.prompt: The dominant market player holds 70% market share in Germany and offers memberships for €70. Would you recommend entering the market?
questions.guidance: Good answer: further investigation is required before a final recommendation. Key question is whether Sosland Sports can differentiate its offering. If the competitor uses a cost-leadership strategy with low-quality service, Sosland could position as a premium provider. Outstanding answer: if the competitor spans all segments (low to high quality) and has a lower cost base, Sosland Sports should not enter — a price war cannot be won. Candidate should recognize that at €90.70 break-even vs. €70 incumbent price, differentiation is essential to justify the premium.

brainstorming.prompt: What could Sosland Sports offer customers to differentiate their service offering?

categories.name: Programming & Instruction
ideas: Provide high-quality squash courses and coaching
Set up cross-country tournaments between Sweden and Germany

categories.name: Marketing & Brand
ideas: Partner with or advertise using celebrities and famous athletes

categories.name: Pricing & Access
ideas: Offer longer opening hours as a premium tier membership benefit

categories.name: Ancillary Services
ideas: Offer a café or bar within the facility
Leverage existing sauna, spa, pool, and gym as differentiators

recommendation: Sosland Sports should only enter the German market if it can credibly differentiate its offering from the dominant incumbent
The break-even membership fee of ~€90/year is already above the incumbent's €70/year fee, meaning Sosland must deliver visible premium value to attract members at that price
risks: Competitor reaction to a new entrant (potential price reduction by incumbent)
Differing consumer preferences and leisure buying habits in Germany vs. Sweden
next_steps: Deeper dive into the dominant competitor's business model, quality tier, and geographic coverage
Market research into German consumers' leisure spending habits and willingness to pay a premium for squash facilities
